Based on the Fedora patch (https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/openssh/pull-request/105), but we preserve the strcmp check before calling getpwnam to keep the happy path fast and reliable.

I also pulled in a change from a later stonking merge to fix the i386 tests.

diff --git a/debian/patches/lp-2150273-openssh-pam-upn.patch b/debian/patches/lp-2150273-openssh-pam-upn.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a1fa084
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/lp-2150273-openssh-pam-upn.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+Description: Fix PAM user mismatch with alternative UPN suffixes
+ OpenSSH >= 10.1 rejects a login when a PAM module canonicalises PAM_USER
+ to a name that differs from the one the session started with.
+Author: Finn Rayk Gartner <finn.gartner@canonical.com>
+Bug: https://bugzilla.mindrot.org/show_bug.cgi?id=3955
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/openssh/+bug/2150273
+Last-Update: 2026-08-04
+---
+--- a/auth-pam.c
++++ b/auth-pam.c
+@@ -481,6 +481,7 @@
+ check_pam_user(Authctxt *authctxt)
+ {
+ 	const char *pam_user;
++	const struct passwd *pam_pw;
+ 
+ 	if (authctxt == NULL || authctxt->pw == NULL ||
+ 	    authctxt->pw->pw_name == NULL)
+@@ -497,7 +498,10 @@
+ 
+ 	if (sshpam_initial_user == NULL)
+ 		fatal_f("internal error: sshpam_initial_user NULL");
+-	if (strcmp(sshpam_initial_user, pam_user) != 0) {
++	if (strcmp(sshpam_initial_user, pam_user) == 0)
++		return PAM_SUCCESS;
++	pam_pw = getpwnam(pam_user);
++	if (pam_pw == NULL || pam_pw->pw_uid != authctxt->pw->pw_uid) {
+ 		error_f("PAM user \"%s\" does not match previous \"%s\"",
+ 		      pam_user, sshpam_initial_user);
+ 		return PAM_USER_UNKNOWN;
